ai.description: The Indian Toad (Bufonidae) grows to 6–8 cm. It is yellowish-brown with dark spots and a distinct, thin, light-colored vertebral stripe. Key features include prominent parotoid glands and warty skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Duttaphrynus parietalis* is best identified by the prominent, elongated, and smooth parotoid glands that extend well behind the eyes, lacking the distinct cranial crests.
ai.habitat: The Indian toad inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at altitudes ranging from 500 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dusk to forage for insects and small invertebrates across forest floors and human-altered landscapes.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus parietalis* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in long, gelatinous strings in water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian toad (*Duttaphrynus parietalis*) is endemic to the Western Ghats, occurring across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Maharashtra from sea level to 1,500m.
ai.callDescription: The Indian Toad emits a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "chirp" notes, typically heard calling from rocky streams or forest floors during the monsoon season.
